stories.title: BATHOGEN: a dataset of bat-associated pathogens to support zoonotic disease surveillance initiatives in Brazil
stories.description: Bats are hosts of many pathogens with zoonotic potential. We built a comprehensive database of records of bat-pathogen associations in Brazil to support zoonotic disease surveillance initiatives. A systematic search across several free-access databases and specialized digital repositories was conducted to compile this dataset, which contains 1,829 records of bat-associated pathogens, including 1,221 pathogen taxa and 111 bat taxa. Viruses were present in most associations, followed by bacteria, fungi, and protozoa. The highest number of pathogen records was found in phyllostomid frugivorous bats. Bat species Artibeus lituratus, Carollia perspicillata, Desmodus rotundus, and Molossus molossus present the highest numbers of associations with pathogens (bacteria, fungi, protozoans, and viruses). Southeastern and Southern Brazil presented the highest pathogen diversity, which is possibly related to the effort and ease of surveying in these regions, whereas the Central, Northern, and Northeastern regions showed the lowest diversity. Our dataset is a single open-source dataset built to support zoonosis surveillance systems in Brazil and is also useful for wildlife health, epidemiology, disease ecology, biodiversity, and species conservation.

stories.title: Transcriptomic changes in tomato plants infected with ToBRFV after cold air glow discharge plasma treatment
stories.description: Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) is an emerging tobamovirus that poses a serious threat to global tomato production. In this study, we evaluated the potential of cold air glow discharge plasma (CAGDP) as a seed treatment to mitigate ToBRFV infection and induce systemic resistance in tomato plants. RNA-Seq analysis of ToBRFV-infected leaves from CAGDP-treated and untreated plants revealed significant transcriptional reprogramming. Compared to infected controls, CAGDP treatment led to the downregulation of 1237 and upregulation of 470 transcripts (|fold change| > 2, FDR < 0.05). Gene ontology (GO) enrichment highlighted the involvement of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in oxidation-reduction processes, metabolic pathways, and defense-related cellular components. KEGG pathway analysis further indicated activation of key defense mechanisms, including plant-pathogen interaction, MAPK signaling, hormone signal transduction, and biosynthesis of secondary metabolites. Notably, CAGDP treatment enhanced the expression of genes associated with antioxidant activity and antiviral responses, while suppressing several uncharacterized and stress-related transcripts, including members of the HSP20 and nodulin-like families. RT-qPCR validation confirmed the reliability of RNA-seq data. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that CAGDP not only reduces viral accumulation but also primes the plant’s immune system through coordinated transcriptomic shifts. This study provides a molecular foundation for using non-thermal plasma as a sustainable strategy to manage ToBRFV and potentially other viral diseases in crops.
